payload.title: pr_tracking._mark_beliefs_for_revalidation is a second writer of memory/beliefs.jsonl that skips the owner's freshness stamp, stale threshold and confidence decay, so a belief reopened by a merge keeps its original anchor commit and repo state, never turns stale through this path, and the evidence_invalidated journal row records that old anchor

payload.rule_violated: One writer per ledger with one set of transition rules (memory._stamp_belief_freshness contract, memory.STALE_AFTER_REVALIDATION_CYCLES; CLAUDE.md Single center, no duplicates)
payload.notes: A merge that touches a file a belief cites reaches this writer in a standard cycle. Probed at d716541239 with a belief at needs_revalidation_cycles=5, confidence 0.9, repo_state_id rs-OLD: the appended row has status needs_revalidation (the memory writers write stale from 3 cycles), confidence 0.9, repo_state_id rs-OLD and the old base_commit_sha, and the evidence_invalidated learning event for cycle cyc-NEW carries the same old anchor. A belief that merges keep breaking therefore never goes stale through this path, and the journal misdates the anchor of the transition. Close condition: Route the revalidation row through the one belief-row writer in memory.py (stamp freshness, apply STALE_AFTER_REVALIDATION_CYCLES and the decayed confidence) and remove memory/beliefs.jsonl from pr_tracking's surface map; add a test that after _mark_beliefs_for_revalidation a belief at 3 or more revalidation cycles is stale, its repo_state_id and base_commit_sha are the current cycle's, and the journal row carries those values. Plan row: F1.1 (the reader half of ARIA-LOW-732 stays with F1.2). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
